chunks: From him, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about a man who had children and married off two of them, and specified the dowry (sadaq) for them, then he died. From where is the dowry calculated: from the total wealth or from their shares? He said: 'From all the wealth, for it is in the position of a debt.'

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the Two Imams (referring to Imam al-Baqir or Imam al-Sadiq)
key_terms.الدَّيْن: Debt, indicating a prior claim on the estate
key_terms.الصَّدَاق: Dowry or bridal price specified in marriage contract

ai.seo_question: How is a father's obligation to pay dowry for his children handled upon his death in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the dowry (sadaq) of married children is treated as a general debt (dayn) against the deceased father's entire estate, rather than being limited to the specific shares of the married heirs. This ruling ensures that the dowry is paid in full before the distribution of inheritance, reflecting the principle that marital obligations are prioritized claims on the estate. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining the order of settlement among various debts and bequests.
